top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock is a distinct idea from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and its 10^-18 performance is a measured, independently reproduced fact (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE). The two-name allocation to Katori and Ye is coherent (concept and first demonstration, then the accuracy frontier), and a citation limited to the lattice and the 10^-18 regime keeps the prospective fundamental-physics payoff out of the operative clause. My reservations (refinement of an honoured programme, other contributors such as Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Bloom, priority still to be checked by external experts) are real but do not outweigh awarding a verified achievement over no award.
